module1Welcome.title: Welcome to Fresh Nest Co.
module1Welcome.sec1: Fresh Nest Co. provides cleaning and organizing services to homes across Cornwall, Akwesasne, Snye, Long Sault, and Morrisburg. Our clients trust us with their homes, and that trust is earned through reliability, respect, and consistent quality on every visit.
module1Welcome.sec2: As a Fresh Nest Co. team member, you're expected to arrive on time for every shift, communicate through the FSM app, and treat every client home with the same care you'd give your own. Lauren and the team are here to support you — reach out anytime you have a question.

q1.question: What five communities does Fresh Nest Co. serve?
q1.choiceB: Cornwall, Akwesasne, Snye, Long Sault, and Morrisburg

q2.question: What is the most important thing clients trust Fresh Nest Co. with?

q3.question: How should you communicate about your shifts?

module2AppTraining.title: Using the Fresh Nest App
module2AppTraining.sec1: The Shift Board shows available shifts you can claim based on your availability and travel constraints. Once you claim or are assigned a shift, it's your responsibility to arrive on time and complete the scheduled clean.
module2AppTraining.sec2: Check in as soon as you arrive at the client property, and check out once every task is complete. Geotagging confirms your arrival time and protects you if a client ever disputes when you were there.
module2AppTraining.sec3: Every job has a checklist of required tasks. Some tasks — like deep-cleaning the stove or main bathroom fixtures — require a verification photo. You can't check out of a job until the checklist is complete.

q1.question: What confirms your arrival time at a client property?

q2.question: Can you check out of a job with an incomplete checklist?
q2.choiceC: No — checklist completion is required before checkout

q3.question: What do high-value checklist tasks require in addition to being completed?
q3.choiceB: A phone call to the client

module3CleaningTechniques.title: Cleaning Techniques by Surface
module3CleaningTechniques.sec1: Always clean top to bottom and dry to wet — dust and debris fall, so start with ceiling fans and shelves before floors, and vacuum before mopping. This avoids re-cleaning surfaces you already finished.
module3CleaningTechniques.sec2: Different surfaces need different care: hardwood floors should never be soaked, stainless steel should be wiped in the direction of the grain to avoid streaking, and glass and mirrors need a lint-free cloth. When in doubt about a surface, ask before using a product you're unsure of.

q1.question: What order should you clean a room in?
q1.choiceA: Top to bottom, dry to wet
q1.choiceB: Bottom to top, wet to dry

q2.question: How should stainless steel be wiped to avoid streaking?
q2.choiceB: In the direction of the grain
q2.choiceC: With as much water as possible

q3.question: What should you do if you're unsure whether a product is safe for a surface?
q3.choiceB: Skip the surface entirely without telling anyone

module4Whmis.title: Chemical Safety — WHMIS
module4Whmis.sec1: WHMIS (Workplace Hazardous Materials Information System) is Ontario law for any worker who handles hazardous products — including the cleaning chemicals you use every shift. Every product you use must have a label and a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) that explains its hazards and safe handling.
module4Whmis.sec2: WHMIS pictograms on product labels warn you about specific hazards — flammability, corrosion, health hazards, and more. Read the label before using any product you haven't used before, and never remove or deface a product's original label.
module4Whmis.sec3: Never mix cleaning chemicals — combining bleach and ammonia-based products, for example, creates toxic gas. Always use products in a well-ventilated area, and wear gloves when a label instructs you to. If you're ever unsure about a product, stop and ask before using it.

q1.question: What must every hazardous cleaning product have, by law?
q1.choiceB: A label and a Safety Data Sheet (SDS)

q2.question: What do WHMIS pictograms on a label tell you?

q3.question: Is it ever safe to mix bleach and ammonia-based cleaners?
q3.choiceC: No — it creates toxic gas and must never be done

module5ClientStandards.title: Client Home Standards
module5ClientStandards.sec1: You're a guest in every client's home. Respect their privacy — don't open drawers, closets, or areas outside your checklist, and never use a client's phone, food, or belongings without permission.
module5ClientStandards.sec2: Communicate clearly: let the client know when you've arrived and when you're finishing up, if that's part of the job. If a client asks for something outside your checklist, don't improvise — let them know you'll pass the request to Lauren.
module5ClientStandards.sec3: Access codes and keys are confidential. Never share a client's door code or lockbox combination with anyone, and always make sure the home is locked and secure before you leave.

q1.question: What should you do if a client asks you to do something outside your checklist?
q1.choiceA: Let them know you'll pass the request to Lauren
q1.choiceB: Do it anyway without telling anyone

q2.question: Can you use a client's phone or food without asking?

q3.question: What must you do with a client's door code or lockbox combination?
q3.choiceA: Share it with other cleaners for convenience
q3.choiceB: Post it in the FSM app notes
q3.choiceC: Keep it confidential and never share it

module6EmergencyProcedures.title: When Things Go Wrong
module6EmergencyProcedures.sec1: If you accidentally break or damage something, don't hide it — report it through the FSM app and to Lauren right away. Honest, immediate reporting is always the right call and protects you.
module6EmergencyProcedures.sec2: If a client is upset or disputes something about the clean, stay calm and don't argue. Listen, let them know you'll pass their concern to Lauren, and end the interaction professionally.
module6EmergencyProcedures.sec3: In a medical emergency, call 911 first, then notify Lauren as soon as it's safe to do so. For any other urgent issue on a job — a lockout, an unsafe condition, anything that stops you from finishing safely — contact Lauren immediately.

q1.question: What should you do if you accidentally damage something in a client's home?
q1.choiceA: Report it through the app and to Lauren right away
q1.choiceB: Hide it and hope no one notices
q1.choiceC: Fix it yourself without telling anyone

q2.question: How should you respond if a client disputes something about your clean?
q2.choiceA: Argue until they agree with you
q2.choiceB: Stay calm, listen, and pass the concern to Lauren

q3.question: In a medical emergency on the job, what's the first thing you should do?
q3.choiceB: Text Lauren and wait for a reply

terms.title: Terms of Service & Workplace Guidelines
terms.subtitle: Please review and accept our latest guidelines before continuing.
terms.checkbox: I have read, understood, and agree to follow these Terms of Service and Workplace Guidelines.
terms.sec1Text: Cleaners are expected to claim shifts from the Shift Board that align with their availability and travel constraints. Once a shift is claimed or assigned, it is the cleaner's responsibility to arrive on time and complete the scheduled clean.
terms.sec2Text: All staff must check in using the mobile app immediately upon arrival at the client property and check out once all tasks are completed. Geotagging is enabled to verify arrival times and protect against billing disputes.
terms.sec3Text: Every job includes a mandatory checklist of tasks. Designated high-value tasks (e.g. deep cleaning the stove, primary bathroom fixtures) require uploading verification photos. Checklist completion is mandatory for job checkout.
terms.sec4Text: For staff with monthly earnings limits (e.g. ODSP recipients), the system enforces limits to prevent clawbacks. Bypassing or attempting to manipulate the earnings tracker is strictly prohibited.
